answer: Superlinear identity fees resist sybils: the Nth agent identity costs N-squared units, not a flat rate. One honest agent, call it Pearl, pays 1 unit; a farm spinning up 1,000 fakes (Marble-1 through Marble-1000) owes the sum of n-squared, about 334 million units, not 1,000. The attack only works if the fee stays flat, which turns a cheap sybil fable into a bankrupting bill. Cost grows with the cube of the swarm, so dishonest scale taxes itself.
